title: Base change and composition of smooth morphisms of fixed relative dimension
statement: Let $n,m\geq0$ be integers. Smooth morphisms of relative dimension $n$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] have the following permanence properties. (1) For schemes $X,S,S'$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], a smooth morphism $f:X\to S$ of relative dimension $n$, and any $g:S'\to S$, the projection $X\times_SS'\to S'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is smooth of relative dimension $n$. (2) For schemes $U,X,S$, if $a:U\to X$ is smooth of relative dimension $m$ and $f:X\to S$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$, then $f\circ a$ is smooth of relative dimension $m+n$. Empty schemes are permitted. In particular an etale $a$ has $m=0$.

proof.text: Unpack [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: the supplied smooth maps $f$ and, in clause (2), $a$ are locally of finite presentation and formally smooth. Their respective fibre dimensions at every source point are $n$ and $m$. To check local finite type with the affine-cover definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], fix any affine open $V$ of the target and cover its inverse image by affine opens $W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], the algebra of each $W$ is a quotient of a polynomial algebra in finitely many variables over the algebra of $V$. The images of these variables generate that algebra, so this is the required cover by finitely generated algebras. No finite subcover or quasi-compactness is required.

For clause (1), put $P=X\times_S S\prime$, with projections $p:P\to X$ and $q:P\to S\prime$. To verify formal smoothness of $q$ [def-sbc-formally-smooth], take an affine first-order thickening $i:T\to T\prime$, a map $b:T\prime\to S\prime$, and $t:T\to P$ with $qt=bi$. Formal smoothness of $f$ supplies $v:T\prime\to X$ extending $pt$ and satisfying $fv=gb$. The universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $(v,b):T\prime\to P$; its restriction is $t$, since both projections agree, and its composite with $q$ is $b$. Thus the required lift exists.

source.place: Tag 02H2 (lemma-base-change-formally-smooth), filling in the omitted lifting argument

proof.text: By clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $q$ is locally of finite presentation, since $f$ is and $g$ is arbitrary. Together with the lift just constructed this makes $q$ smooth by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Only the local finite presentation clause is used: none of the quasi-compactness hypotheses in the other clauses is imposed.

For any $z\in P$, let $x=p(z)$ and $s\prime=q(z)$. Apply [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] to the cartesian square defining $P$: its locally finite type hypothesis for $f$ was checked in Step 1, and it allows an arbitrary $g$. It gives $\dim_z(P_{s\prime})=\dim_x(X_{f(x)})=n$. Hence the smooth map $q$ has relative dimension $n$ by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

For clause (2), verify formal smoothness of $f\circ a$ directly using [def-sbc-formally-smooth]. Given an affine first-order thickening $i:T\to T\prime$, $b:T\prime\to S$, and $t:T\to U$ with $fat=bi$, first lift $at:T\to X$ through $f$ to $v:T\prime\to X$ with $vi=at$ and $fv=b$. Now regard the same thickening as one over $X$ via $v$ and lift $t$ through $a$ to $w:T\prime\to U$ with $wi=t$ and $aw=v$. Then $faw=b$, which is exactly the requested lift.

source.place: Tag 02H1 (lemma-composition-formally-smooth), filling in the omitted two-lift argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition] to $a$ and $f$, whose local finite presentation was extracted in Step 1. Thus $f\circ a$ is locally of finite presentation; together with Step 5, [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] says it is smooth.

By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], the smooth map $a$ is flat. For each $u\in U$ put $x=a(u)$ and $s=f(x)$, and apply [lem-sbc-flat-composite-fibre-dimension-at-point]; both maps are locally finite type by Step 1, and $a$ is flat at $u$. The result is $\dim_u(U_s)=\dim_u(U_x)+\dim_x(X_s)=m+n$. Since Step 6 proves smoothness, [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] now gives relative dimension $m+n$ for $f\circ a$.

No step chooses a point without first quantifying over the source. If $P$ or $U$ is empty the fibre-dimension assertions are vacuous, and the lifting arguments remain valid: they start with a supplied map $T$ into that source. If $a$ is etale, [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] defines it to be smooth of relative dimension zero, so Step 7 gives $0+n=n$.
